did_you_know.text: Lime is an ancient building material made by heating limestone, and it was used as white plaster. Coating the stones created a smooth surface for writing.
The prohibition against using iron when building the altar also appears in Exodus. It emphasizes that the altar was to be made of natural stones, not shaped with a weapon-like tool.
A peace offering was also a meal shared by the participants, not merely a sacrifice that was burned. It expressed gratitude and shared joy before God.
The phrase “explain clearly” means that the message should be made very understandable. It was not meant to remain obscure or accessible only to a few.
The word hasket is a rare biblical verb, generally understood to mean paying close attention and listening carefully. It introduces an important public declaration.
Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal face each other in the Shechem area, near today’s city of Nablus. Their geography made it possible to hold a ceremony heard from both sides of the valley.
A pesel usually refers to an image carved from a material, while a massekah is an image cast in a mold. The two words describe different kinds of idols.
In ancient times, boundary stones marked the size of a piece of land. Moving them secretly was a way to take part of a neighbor’s property without being noticed immediately.

The word amen is related to the Hebrew root א־מ־ן, expressing firmness and trustworthiness. Saying amen here is a public affirmation and acceptance of responsibility, not merely a momentary agreement.
